title: Why Your House Gets Dusty So Fast in Las Cruces
metaTitle: Why Homes Get Dusty So Fast in Las Cruces
metaDescription: Outdoor dust, spring wind, open windows, and cooling systems add to indoor dust in Las Cruces. Reduce what enters, then clean from high to low.
summary: Outdoor dust, open windows, and cooling systems add to the normal dust made indoors. Reduce what enters first, then clean from high to low.
transcript: Homes in the Mesilla Valley deal with plenty of outdoor dust, especially when spring winds pick up. That doesn't mean you're cleaning wrong. It means the house has a steady supply to manage.

Some dust is made indoors by cooking, fabric fibers, skin, pets, and ordinary activity. The rest comes through doors, open windows, small gaps, and cooling systems that bring in outdoor air. An evaporative cooler creates a more direct connection to outside than refrigerated air, but no house is sealed well enough to keep every particle out.

Start by reducing what enters. Put a coarse mat outside the doors people use and a washable mat just inside. Removing shoes helps too, especially after yard work or a windy day. Clean the mats regularly or they become another dust source.

Check exterior doors and windows for obvious gaps. If you can see daylight around a closed door, replace or adjust the weatherstripping. During a wind event, keep doors and windows closed when your cooling system allows it. If you use an evaporative cooler, don't close its required exhaust path. Follow the manufacturer's instructions for your setup.

If the home has a central refrigerated-air system, inspect the filter regularly and replace it according to the equipment and filter manufacturer. The EPA recommends MERV 13, or the highest rating the system can accommodate. A filter that is too restrictive for the fan can create a different problem, so don't choose by number alone. Evaporative cooler pads are separate equipment and should be maintained as the manufacturer directs.

Once the supply is under control, clean in an order that keeps you from doing the same room twice. Turn fans off. Start with fan blades, high shelves, frames, blinds, and furniture. Vacuum upholstery and rugs next. Vacuum floors, then damp mop washable hard flooring last.

Use a barely damp microfiber cloth on surfaces that tolerate moisture. A feather duster or dry cloth can move fine particles back into the air, where they settle again after you're finished. Fold the cloth to expose a clean side and rinse or replace it before it starts leaving streaks.

Soft surfaces hold more than they show. Curtains, upholstery, rugs, pet beds, and bedding release dust when someone sits down or a fan starts. Clean each item according to its care label instead of soaking fabric or using an attachment that could damage it.

A portable air cleaner can reduce airborne particles in one room if it is sized for the space and run long enough. It won't remove dust that has already settled, and it doesn't replace source control or surface cleaning. Avoid devices that intentionally produce ozone.

If dust suddenly gets worse, appears in streaks below a vent, or returns within hours in one room, look for a specific source. A damaged filter, poorly seated filter, dirty cooler pad, duct leak, construction work, or gap at an exterior opening may need attention before another cleaning helps.
localNote: High winds are common here in spring, and a blowing-dust day can undo hours of work. Close the house as much as your cooling system safely allows, wait for the event to pass, then clean. Chasing dust while it is still coming in is usually wasted effort.

faq.q: Am I doing something wrong if the dust is back in two days?
faq.a: Not necessarily. Check the main entry, open windows, filter or cooler pads, and soft furnishings before changing every cleaning product. A steady source will beat a better duster every time.

Yes, for airborne particles in the room where the unit is running. Choose one sized for the space and avoid ozone-producing models. It won't remove the dust already sitting on floors, curtains, or furniture.

faq.q: Is a feather duster ever fine?
faq.a: It can handle a very light weekly pass, but microfiber is better for visible buildup because it holds the particles instead of scattering them. Use a damp cloth only on surfaces that tolerate moisture.

Start at the entrance used most often: use mats outside and inside, clean them regularly, and leave dusty shoes at the door. If air or dust is coming through a visible gap, fix the weatherstripping next.
